title.narrative: Activity under preparation Efficient Water Resilience

description.narrative: The water sector is at the front-line of economic development and climate adaptation in Tajikistan, as policy makers must address competing demands from irrigated agriculture, hydro-power, industry, and municipalities. Better water resource management and strategic investments in modernizing the water sector¿s irrigation infrastructure and institutions will be critical in the face of rising economic, demographic, and climate pressures. An improved water policy at the internal and international level is a key objective for the Government of Tajikistan and would be seen as proof of support to the Water Action Decade ¿Water for Sustainable Development¿ 2018-2028 and the supporting Dushanbe Water Process, led by Tajikistan. The country has adopted an Integrated Water Resources Management Approach in its recently-adopted Water Strategy (November 2024). The Water Strategy follows many aspects of the EU policy approach enshrined in the Water Directive and, notably the river basin approach, which has been successful in the parts of the country where it has been applied. The Government of Tajikistan has actively asked the EU to continue its infrastructure and technical advice support, including directly to the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources, which, along with our support in the field of energy, has a direct impact in the preparation of policy and legislation.The agricultural sector is the third-largest energy consumer, accounting for 20.5% of Tajikistan¿s summer electricity demand. However, it largely fails to cover its own expenses (despite very low tariffs). A vicious circle is set in motion, whereby both the water, agriculture and energy sectors suffer. The country¿s pumping infrastructure is complex in design and is technically aging. Some pressure pipelines, for instance, have been in operation for over fifty years and are characterized by water leakages. The action is intended to enhance water resilience by reconciling the water-energy-food-environment nexus trade-offs into a viable, gender responsive, efficient and adaptable business model, integrating various considerations, namely the production of energy from hydro-power generation, and its use through irrigation, promoting a sustainable land management. Furthermore, the action promotes Climate Change adaptation by achieving greater levels of water security, through improved efficiency of irrigation systems and more effective use of water resources.The Overall Objective of the Action is to improve irrigation water management and energy consumption to contribute to the enabling environment for institutions and business development in agriculture.Specific Objectives of this action are: S.O.1. To support selected energy-saving infrastructures investment in water supply for irrigation systems; S.O.2. To support the establishment of public incentives for private investments in new technologies and methods for on-farm irrigation; S.O.3. To provide Capacity building to support irrigation water demand management, improving effectiveness and operational efficiency and implementing nature-based solutions and reforestation for sustainable development particularly in managing water resources.
